🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin steadies above $84K as oil eases, but ETF outflows, a hardware-wallet supply-chain scare and Wednesday's CPI print keep traders cautious. In Washington, crypto rules now run through agencies and courts, not Congress. 📈 Bitcoin Holds Above $84,000 Despite $600M+ ETF Outflows Bitcoin is holding on to its weekend gains above $84,000 as oil prices slide, even though U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs bled more than $600 million in outflows last week. Altcoins are leading the bounce, with ether and solana each up more than 2% on the day. Read full story 🕵️ Ledger Confirms Unauthorized Implant in CryptoBilis-Sold Device Ledger says an unauthorized implant was found in at least one hardware wallet sold by CryptoBilis, its authorized reseller for Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines. Sales were paused on Oct. 9 after on-chain investigators estimated around $86M in user losses; Ledger urges recent CryptoBilis buyers not to set up their devices and to move funds to a new device with a fresh seed, while stressing its own systems were not compromised. More details 🐞 Inside the Hidden XRP Ledger Bug That Threatened the 100B Supply Cap A new deep dive examines how a decade-old XRP Ledger flaw, which could have created billions of dollars' worth of XRP from nothing, went undetected for years before being patched. The episode reopens questions about auditing legacy code in long-running blockchains. Read more ⚖️ Prediction Markets Edge Toward a Supreme Court Showdown States and platforms alike now want the U.S. Supreme Court to decide whether sports event contracts are state-regulated gambling or CFTC-regulated swaps. The push comes days after the CFTC moved to fold event contracts into its swaps rules as the legal fight intensifies. See details 🏛️ CLARITY Act's Collapse Hands the Crypto Rulebook to Regulators With the market-structure bill dead after a 49–50 Senate cloture vote, U.S. crypto policy now rests on SEC and CFTC rulemaking. Analysis suggests that path could speed innovation while favoring incumbents; comments on the SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets close October 20.
